clue.text: Key functions of passenger vehicles

parts.note: B is a musical key
uses are functions or purposes

explanation.surface: A question about the main roles of buses and coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key functions' reads as 'main purposes'; in fact 'Key' gives the musical key B and 'functions' gives USES.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses are large road transport carrying the public.

clue.text: Constantly tapped in lobby, shows the pressure

definitions.text: Constantly tapped in lobby, shows the pressure

parts.words: Constantly tapped in lobby, shows the pressure
parts.note: sounds like a bugged lobbyist under strain, but it is the hall instrument people tap to read air pressure

explanation.surface: A political lobby under constant phone-tapping shows the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures atmospheric pressure and is traditionally tapped to settle its needle.

clue.text: Cylinder jammed?

parts.note: jammed reads as stuck, but here it means filled with jam: a rolled sponge cake

explanation.surface: An engine cylinder that has seized up.
explanation.definitionFit: This sponge cake is spread with jam and rolled into a log shape.

clue.text: Undistinguished pieces of Picasso's output

indicators.note: pieces of means a fragment is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Dismissing some of Picasso's works as mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or mediocre work is merely passable.

clue.text: Biting what people see on plates-Turkish delight

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle registration code for Turkey, seen on number plates
to enchant is to delight

explanation.surface: A sharp remark about a dish of Turkish delight served on plates.
explanation.walkthrough: TR is the code on Turkish car number plates; 'plates' looks like crockery but means number plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is cutting and incisive, as a biting remark is.

clue.text: Theatrical scout-patrol set tent out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order, so patrol set tent is rearranged

explanation.surface: Boy scouts on patrol pitching a tent outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical agent who looks for promising performers is a scout for new stars.

clue.text: Doubly firm palm-tree

indicators.note: doubly says the following piece is given twice in a row

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A palm tree that is very firmly rooted.
explanation.definitionFit: The coconut palm is a tropical tree.

clue.text: Entertain with calliope, say?

explanation.surface: Someone playing a steam organ to entertain a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A calliope looks like the steam organ; with a capital it is Calliope, one of the nine Muses, so 'Calliope, say' is a Muse.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is to divert someone; Calliope, muse of epic poetry, is one of nine such goddesses.

clue.text: River for hire? Take the temperature first

indicators.note: first says the temperature piece comes before the hire piece

parts.note: to rent is to hire

explanation.surface: A river available for hire, but take its temperature beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is England's third-longest waterway.

clue.text: Tracks of birds

explanation.surface: Footprints left by birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway lines are metal tracks; the rail is also a family of marsh birds such as the water rail.

clue.text: Sea-locust evolving? That has no chance of success!

definitions.text: That has no chance of success!

indicators.note: evolving means changing form, so the letters of sea-locust are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scoff at the idea that a sea creature might develop further.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless cause is a venture certain to fail.

clue.text: Number one life cover taken with aplomb?

parts.note: looking after number one means looking after oneself
life assurance is insurance cover on a life

explanation.surface: Someone buying life insurance for themselves with confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is calm confidence in oneself.

clue.text: Body service

explanation.surface: A two-word pairing of a corpse and a church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass is a body of matter, and the Mass is the Eucharist church service.

clue.text: Corner sometimes obtuse?

explanation.surface: A remark that someone in a corner can be slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner is where two lines meet at an angle; angles over ninety degrees are called obtuse.

clue.text: Run and hide

explanation.surface: Advice to a fugitive: flee and conceal yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To pelt is to run fast, and a pelt is an animal's skin or hide.

clue.text: Warms up for sections of contest

explanation.surface: An athlete warming up for the rounds of a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat is to warm; heats are the preliminary rounds of a race.

clue.text: Spirit kept in bottle for ages?

definitions.text: Spirit kept in bottle for ages?

parts.words: Spirit kept in bottle for ages?
parts.note: spirit reads as an aged whisky, but it is the magic being trapped in a lamp or bottle

explanation.surface: Whisky that has been aged in the bottle for years.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinn is a supernatural spirit of Arabian folklore, often confined in a lamp or bottle.

clue.text: Inflation closed account

parts.note: something over is finished or closed
a statement is an account, as in a bank statement

explanation.surface: A finance note about inflation and a closed bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' reads as rising prices but means exaggeration.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflating a story by exaggeration makes it an overblown claim.

clue.text: Sissy eats cooked bacon and lamb, we hear

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so the letters of sissy eats are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fussy eater tucking into bacon and lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon and Charles Lamb were English prose writers; 'we hear' admits that bacon and lamb only sound like the writers, since the capitals are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon and Charles Lamb were both famous writers of short prose pieces.

clue.text: Spectacles on bridge, covering three fields?

definitions.text: Spectacles on bridge, covering three fields?

parts.words: Spectacles on bridge, covering three fields?
parts.note: spectacles sit on the bridge of the nose; these lenses have three focal zones, read as covering three fields of view

explanation.surface: A grand show staged on a bridge spanning three meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses with three lens sections serve near, middle and distance vision.

clue.text: Affairs in which antihero slips away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters go off and astray, so antihero slips is rearranged

explanation.surface: A love story in which the flawed protagonist sneaks off.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic affairs are liaisons between partners.

clue.text: Every single youth-leader a companion?

parts.note: every single one means all

indicators.note: the leader of the word youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether every young leader has a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion who sides with you is a friend or partner.

clue.text: Troublesome insect took cover under a piano

indicators.note: under says in this down clue the took-cover piece sits below the others

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
hid means took cover

explanation.surface: A pest that hid beneath a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking garden pests.

clue.text: Water-plant much seen over America?

indicators.note: seen over says in this down clue the much piece stands above the America piece

parts.note: a lot means much
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A pond plant that is common across America.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred lily of Asia is an aquatic flowering species.

clue.text: Street paintings can give a shock

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Street art can be shocking to passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or startle with surprise.

clue.text: Beginner helping to make pretty rockery

indicators.note: helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A novice gardener lending a hand to build an attractive rock garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or learner is someone new to a skill.

clue.text: Foreign coin of Arnold Bennett's girl

explanation.surface: A heroine of an Arnold Bennett novel with a foreign coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former Indian coin; Anna Tellwright is the heroine of Bennett's novel Anna of the Five Towns.

clue.text: Kind of singing from southern jazz-fan?

parts.note: cat is slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A style of singing heard from a jazz lover in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised vocal jazz using nonsense syllables is a singing style.

clue.text: Road accident more serious than touch-and-go?

definitions.text: Road accident more serious than touch-and-go?

parts.words: Road accident more serious than touch-and-go?
parts.note: a hit is worse than a touch and running off worse than going, so the crash where the driver flees is one up on touch-and-go

explanation.surface: A car crash that is graver than a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision where the driver strikes someone and flees the scene is this kind of crime.

clue.text: Conspirator from whom Caesar took the highest rent?

definitions.text: Conspirator from whom Caesar took the highest rent?

parts.words: Conspirator from whom Caesar took the highest rent?
parts.note: rent as a tear or stab wound, not a payment: this plotter struck Caesar first, at the neck, the highest wound

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor collecting the most rent from a schemer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar and in Suetonius, this conspirator strikes the first blow, at Caesar's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Servilius Casca was one of the senators who plotted Julius Caesar's assassination.

clue.text: Underworld standard time? Rubbish!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
par is a standard or norm
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing talk of a criminal underworld's standard time as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' looks like an exclamation of disbelief but is the verb meaning to belittle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish something is to belittle or criticise it scornfully.

clue.text: Pair positioned forward in jumbo

parts.note: jumbo reads as a jet with two seats up front, but it is an elephant, whose ivory pair juts out in front

explanation.surface: Two passengers seated at the front of a jumbo jet.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long ivory teeth project forward from its mouth.
